title: Distributed consensus and the Raft protocol
description: Leader elections, randomized timeouts, log matching invariants, quorums, and split-brain prevention in Raft.

questions.text: In Raft, why are election timeouts randomized across nodes (e.g. between 150ms and 300ms)?

options.text: To prevent split votes where multiple candidates simultaneously declare candidacy and split the majority quorum
To reduce network bandwidth consumption between follower heartbeats
To allow Byzantine faulty nodes to be detected and isolated
To balance CPU utilization evenly across the cluster

questions.explanation: Randomized election timeouts ensure that typically only one follower times out first, increments its term, and gathers a majority before others time out, preventing indefinite split-vote stalemates.

questions.text: What is the Raft Log Matching Invariant?

options.text: Every node must have the exact same number of uncommitted log entries at all times
If two entries in different logs have the same index and term, they store the same command and their logs are identical in all preceding entries
The leader only accepts writes if all follower logs match its log bit-for-bit
Follower logs must always be strictly longer than the candidate's log

questions.explanation: The Log Matching Invariant guarantees that if two logs agree on an entry at index `i` with term `t`, then all prior entries up to `i` are identical. AppendEntries consistency checks enforce this induction.

questions.text: A network partition splits a 5-node Raft cluster into a minority partition of 2 nodes (including the current leader L1) and a majority partition of 3 nodes. What happens when clients send writes to L1?

options.text: L1 commits the writes locally and acknowledges success to clients immediately
L1 crashes and shuts down immediately
L1 accepts the write into its uncommitted log but cannot commit it because it cannot reach a majority quorum (3 nodes), so it never acknowledges success
The minority partition promotes a second leader and splits the state machine permanently

questions.explanation: To commit an entry, a leader must replicate it to a strict majority ($\lfloor N/2 \rfloor + 1 = 3$ nodes). In the minority partition of 2 nodes, L1 cannot reach 3 acknowledgments, so writes remain uncommitted and safe.

questions.text: When a Raft follower receives a RequestVote RPC from candidate C, under which condition MUST the follower refuse to vote for C?

options.text: If candidate C's log is less up-to-date than the follower's own log (lower last term, or same term with fewer entries)
If candidate C has a higher node ID than the follower
If candidate C has sent more than 3 heartbeats in the current term
If candidate C's term number is greater than the follower's term

questions.explanation: Raft's Leader Completeness Property requires that any elected leader contains all committed entries. Followers reject candidate votes if the candidate's log is less up-to-date than their own.

questions.text: In Raft, a leader may directly commit an uncommitted log entry from a previous term once it is replicated on a majority of nodes.
questions.explanation: False (Raft Section 5.4.2). Raft never commits prior-term entries by simply counting replicas; doing so can lead to committed entries being overwritten after leader crashes. A leader only commits entries from its CURRENT term by counting replicas; prior entries are committed indirectly by the Log Matching Property.
